subject: Discovery recap: Observability & eval success criteria for Ava Health
messages:
From: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@avahealth.com>
To: rachel.kim@redwood.ai, neha.kapoor@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-27T15:12:00Z
Subject: Quick follow-up & security packet (thanks for the demo)

Thanks again for the demo earlier today — appreciate the concise walkthrough. A quick recap from our side and a couple of asks so we can line up internal stakeholders:

Pain points we mentioned:
- High token spend on bursty triage workflows (esp. during end-of-day processing)
- No centralized visibility into prompt-level regressions after model rollouts
- Hard to correlate latency spikes with specific prompts / user cohorts

Immediate goals:
1) Run a short eval to compare response quality and unit cost for our triage models
2) Get tracing hooks and dashboards so our SRE and ML teams can monitor regressions
3) Establish a rollout guardrail for model switches (canary + auto-fallback)

Current stack: internal LLM orchestration (homegrown), Kafka for events, Datadog for infra metrics, BigQuery for logs.

I've attached our standard security questionnaire and invited Legal on copy. Can you send a short recap of success criteria + proposed eval plan and any dashboard templates? Also share a proposed timeline for a 2-week proof-of-concept.

— Jordan
Director of Platform Engineering
Ava Health

Attachment: security-questionnaire.pdf

From: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Myers <jordan.myers@avahealth.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwood.ai, sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-06-27T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & security packet (thanks for the demo) — recap + next steps

Jordan — thanks for the clear summary. Below is a concise recap of our call, proposed success criteria, and next steps. I attached a one-pager that summarizes what we discussed (discovery-one-pager.pdf).

Recap of pain points (confirming):
- Cost volatility on bursty token usage during nightly triage jobs
- Lack of observability at prompt/golden-prompt level for post-rollout regression detection
- Need for low-latency fallbacks and predictable SLAs during peak windows

Proposed success criteria for the eval (we'll refine with your team):
- Latency: P95 generation latency <= 300ms for 512-token prompts under expected load profile
- Cost: 20–30% reduction in unit cost vs. your current baseline for the triage workload (measured tokens/response)
- Quality: no >5% drop in task-specific accuracy on your golden prompt set during switchover
- Observability: dashboards showing prompt-level throughput, per-prompt latency, regression alerting tied to golden-prompt fail rates

Recommended eval scope (2-week):
Week 0 (prep): instrumentation + tracing hooks, import golden prompts, baseline measurements
Week 1: run parallel traffic on a sample (10–20% traffic mirroring), capture metrics and trace spans
Week 2: canary rollout of model variant, exercise rollback/fallback, produce final report

Dashboards & tracing we will provide:
- Prompt-level latency/throughput per route
- Golden-prompt result pass/fail trend + alerting thresholds
- KV cache hit rates and per-model memory metrics
- Cost-per-response breakdown by model variant and batching settings

Ask: please confirm the internal owners for the eval (SRE, ML lead, product owner) and any blackout windows for the triage jobs. Also confirm Legal's questions from the attached security doc and whether we should route the questionnaire to procurement.

Next steps I propose:
- Tech deep-dive (SRE + ML) — Thu, 2027-07-01 at 15:00 ET (45m) — I'll send a calendar invite
- We will share an eval playbook (eval-playbook.xlsx) and a sample dashboard link prior to the deep-dive
- Goal: start instrumentation the week of 2027-07-05

Thanks — looking forward to partnering on this.

Best,
Rachel Kim
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
rachel.kim@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Quick follow-up & security packet — instrumentation & dashboard notes

Jordan — adding some technical details and what we'll deliver for the eval. High-level notes below; I will bring implementation steps to the Thu deep-dive.

Instrumentation & tracing hooks:
- Lightweight request trace header (x-rw-trace-id) we ask your services to propagate; Redwood SDK will capture prompt text hash (redacted) + model variant + batch id
- KV cache telemetry emitted as metrics (hit/miss) and optional traces for cache fill events

Dashboards we'll provide (templates):
1) Prompt Health (golden prompts): pass/fail over time, failure reason buckets, and % delta vs baseline
2) Latency Heatmap: per-route P50/P95/P99 with traffic overlay by user cohort
3) Cost Breakdown: per-model tokens in/out, average tokens/response, batching efficiency
4) Rollout Monitor: canary error rate, fallback events, rollback triggers

Regression alerting suggestions:
- Primary alert: golden-prompt fail-rate > 3% over a 30m window OR fail-rate delta > 150% vs baseline
- Secondary: P95 latency > 300ms with sustained increase over 15m and correlated error increase

Eval configuration recommendations:
- Start with a 10% mirrored traffic sample for 3 days to build baseline traces
- Run a 24h canary at 1% traffic, step to 5% if stable, then 10% and validate golden-prompt metrics
- If regression triggers, automatic fallback to previous model and a forensics trace bundle for your ML team

Data/retention answers for Legal: by default eval traces are retained for 30 days. Traces can be redacted on ingest and we can provide access controls; Redwood does not surface raw user PII in dashboards by default. We will include the exact retention and access controls in the SOW addendum.

I'll bring a sample eval-playbook.xlsx to the deep-dive and a pre-populated dashboard link.

— Neha
